label: <DEL> step after a z/e/b/0 in sequences starting with u/p/2/o/a
explanation: Very sparse delimiter unit. About 85% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (phase 1), and most of the rest is on original-phase inputs of z (14% of mass, never at t<2). It never fires during the copy phase. Only about 3% of <DEL> steps fire, though, and which ones depends on two additive factors. The first is the last original token before <DEL>: z and e give about 8x lift, b and 0 about 3x. The second is the first original token: u gives 6x, p/2/o/a 2-3x. It also fires more for mid lengths (L=5-6). Requiring <DEL> AND a favoured last token AND a favoured first token gives dev precision 0.38, recall 0.25, mass recall 0.34. These sequences make up a larger share of the top-quartile activations (37% coverage there vs 15% in the bottom quartile). Using OR instead gives mass recall 0.78 at precision 0.09. Phase==1 alone gives mass recall 0.85 at precision 0.03. No single boolean predicate gets clean precision. The unit looks like a graded sum of token evidence gated to the delimiter step.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=b (+4.11), prev_tok=z (+4.08), prev_tok=e (+4.05), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=z (+3.73), phase=0 & in_tok=z (+3.73), orig1=p (+3.43). Lower it: phase=2 (-7.99), prev_tok=p (-3.44), orig0=z (-3.29), orig0=h (-2.79).
